---
title: "A small example: multi-VAR and adaptive multi-VAR"
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
source("00_load_functions.R")
knitr::opts_chunk$set(message = FALSE, fig.align = "center", out.width = "100%")
```

## 1. Simulate one dataset

Three subjects, five variables, and 80 observations per subject. Each true
transition matrix has two common and two individual nonzero coefficients.
The last three observations are held out.

```{r example-data}
config <- study_config("preliminary", reps = 1L)
settings <- data.frame(
  K = 3L, d = 5L, T = 80L,
  density = 0.16, common_fraction = 0.5,
  sigma = 1, cross_rho = 0, serial_rho = 0,
  measurement_sd = 0, target_radius = 0.8
)
example <- generate_dataset(settings, replication = 1L, config = config)
series <- example$sim$observed
train_end <- settings$T - 3L
training <- lapply(series, function(x) x[seq_len(train_end), , drop = FALSE])
origins <- rolling_origins(settings$T, config$cv_origins)
ratios <- config$ratio_multipliers / settings$K
```

```{r example-series, fig.width=9, fig.height=3.5}
matplot(seq_len(settings$T), series[[1]][, 1:3], type = "l", lty = 1,
        col = c("#0072B2", "#D55E00", "#009E73"),
        xlab = "Time", ylab = "Observed value", main = "Subject 1")
abline(v = train_end + 0.5, lty = 2, col = "grey40")
legend("topright", paste("Variable", 1:3), lty = 1,
       col = c("#0072B2", "#D55E00", "#009E73"),
       bg = "white", box.col = "white", cex = 0.8)
```

## 2. Fit standard multi-VAR as the preliminary estimator

Select penalties using rolling origins `r paste(origins, collapse = ", ")`,
then fit standard multi-VAR to all `r train_end` training observations with FISTA.

```{r fit-multivar}
fit_multivar <- tune_multivar(
  training, origins, config$fractions, ratios,
  custom_final = TRUE
)
```

## 3. Fit adaptive multi-VAR using the preliminary estimates

Construct adaptive weights from the standard multi-VAR subject estimates:
inverse common-median magnitudes and inverse deviations from that median. For validation, refit and tune each preliminary
model. The final adaptive fit uses `fit_multivar`.

```{r fit-adaptive-multivar}
pilots <- fit_multivar_pilots(
  training, origins, config$fractions, ratios,
  final_fit = fit_multivar
)
fit_adaptive <- tune_multivar(
  training, origins, config$fractions, ratios,
  adaptive = TRUE, pilot_fits = pilots
)
fits <- list("Multi-VAR" = fit_multivar, "Adaptive multi-VAR" = fit_adaptive)
```

```{r selected-penalties, echo=FALSE}
tuning <- data.frame(
  Quantity = c("Selected common-penalty fraction ($\\lambda_c/\\lambda_{c,\\max}$)",
               "Individual/common penalty ratio ($r=\\lambda_u/\\lambda_c$)",
               "Common-component penalty ($\\lambda_c$)",
               "Individual-component penalty ($\\lambda_u=r\\lambda_c$)",
               "Minimum mean validation MSE"),
  check.names = FALSE
)
for (method in names(fits)) {
  fit <- fits[[method]]
  tuning[[method]] <- c(fit$fraction, fit$ratio, fit$lambda,
                        fit$ratio * fit$lambda, fit$cv_mse)
}
knitr::kable(tuning, digits = 4, caption = "Selected penalties")
```

For adaptive multi-VAR, these are base penalties; each coefficient's penalty
is additionally multiplied by its adaptive weight.

## 4. Compare coefficient estimates

Subject 1: rows are responses and columns are lagged predictors.

```{r coefficient-comparison, fig.width=12, fig.height=4.5}
matrices <- list(
  "True" = example$truth$A[[1]],
  "Multi-VAR" = t(fit_multivar$B[[1]]),
  "Adaptive multi-VAR" = t(fit_adaptive$B[[1]])
)
d <- settings$d
color_limit <- max(abs(unlist(matrices)))
colors <- colorRampPalette(c("#2166AC", "#FFFFFF", "#B2182B"))(101)
par(mfrow = c(1, 3), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))
for (title in names(matrices)) {
  display <- t(matrices[[title]][d:1, , drop = FALSE])
  image(seq_len(d), seq_len(d), display,
        col = colors, zlim = c(-color_limit, color_limit), axes = FALSE,
        xlab = "Predictor at t-1", ylab = "Response at t", main = title)
  axis(1, at = seq_len(d), labels = paste0("V", seq_len(d)))
  axis(2, at = seq_len(d), labels = paste0("V", d:1), las = 1)
  labels <- ifelse(abs(display) < 0.005, "0.00", sprintf("%.2f", display))
  text(rep(seq_len(d), times = d), rep(seq_len(d), each = d),
       labels = as.vector(labels), cex = 0.75)
  box()
}
```

## 5. Compare recovery and heldout forecasts

Metrics average over the three subjects.

```{r evaluate-models}
metrics <- lapply(fits, function(fit) {
  evaluate_fit(fit, example$truth, example$sim,
               sigma = settings$sigma, threshold = config$support_threshold)
})
```

```{r comparison-table, echo=FALSE}
metric_names <- c("relative_frobenius", "sensitivity",
                  "specificity", "rmsfe_h1", "rmsfe_h2", "rmsfe_h3")
comparison <- data.frame(
  Metric = c("Relative Frobenius error", "Sensitivity",
             "Specificity", "One-step RMSFE", "Two-step RMSFE", "Three-step RMSFE"),
  check.names = FALSE
)
for (method in names(metrics)) {
  comparison[[method]] <- unname(metrics[[method]][metric_names])
}
knitr::kable(comparison, digits = 3, caption = "Single-dataset comparison")
```

Lower errors and higher sensitivity/specificity are better. This is one
illustrative dataset, not a repeated-simulation comparison.
